clue.text: Cultivate distant surface of Mars

parts.note: something distant is far away

indicators.note: the surface is the outermost layer, so only the first letter of Mars is taken

explanation.surface: A space-farming plan to till the far-off Martian soil.
explanation.definitionFit: To farm land is to work and grow crops on it, which is what cultivating it means.

clue.text: Confess to framing model Jodie, being out of control on the runway

definitions.text: being out of control on the runway

indicators.note: a frame goes round a picture, so the confession word is placed around the model's surname

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police
Jodie Kidd is a British fashion model

explanation.surface: A catwalk drama: someone owns up as model Jodie Kidd loses her footing on the runway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runway' suggests a fashion catwalk, but the definition means an aircraft sliding uncontrollably on an airport runway.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane that skids slides sideways without grip, so skidding describes losing control on a landing strip.

clue.text: Attacks small hill with 1,000 soldiers at the rear

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: the rear of the word soldiers is its final letter

explanation.surface: An army of a thousand assaults a little hill, with troops bringing up the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a position is to attack it in a sudden rush, so storms is a synonym of attacks.

clue.text: Tape 100 like me, endlessly

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
as means like, in the same way

indicators.note: without its end, the setter's word loses its final letter

parts.note: from the setter's point of view, me is the setter of the puzzle

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of a hundred tapes just like themselves, on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'me' often stands for the compiler, here SETTER; 'endlessly' trims its last letter to SETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a cartridge of magnetic tape for recording sound, so it is a tape.

clue.text: Break free, when she gets rid of husband over headland

indicators.note: turned over, so what is left of the woman's word is read backwards
the woman's word drops the husband abbreviation, losing that letter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband, as in genealogies
a cape is a headland jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A wife breaks free, ditching her husband and fleeing over the clifftop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reads as fleeing over the cliff, but in this clue it turns the trimmed pronoun round before the headland is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape is to get away from confinement, which is to break free.

clue.text: Gasp as bottom removed from trousers in New York

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the last letter, which is taken away

parts.note: Americans call trousers pants

explanation.surface: Someone gasps as the seat of their trousers rips off on a New York street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' suggests the seat of the trousers, but it means the last letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To pant is to breathe in short quick gasps, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: British cooking takes a bit of skill with containers

indicators.note: food that is cooking is being transformed, so these letters are rearranged
a bit of the word skill is just its first letter

explanation.surface: British cuisine takes some skill with pots and pans.
explanation.definitionFit: Baskets are woven holders for carrying things, so they are containers.

clue.text: Officer getting memory back with small 2001 computer?

indicators.note: going back means the memory word is read in reverse

parts.note: RAM is computer memory, random-access memory
HAL is the computer in the film 2001: A Space Odyssey

explanation.surface: An officer restores a memory to a little computer like the one in 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: A marshal is an officer of high rank, as in a field marshal or a US federal law officer.

clue.text: In Madrid, sick after doctor left

indicators.note: being sick means being out of sorts, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the doctor letters have left, so they are removed from the city name

explanation.surface: Someone is taken ill in Madrid once the doctor has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing DR from MADRID leaves MAID, which 'sick' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid means in the middle of, so it can replace the preposition in, as in amid the crowd.

clue.text: Impervious to nastiest crook stalking queen

indicators.note: to stalk is to follow, so the queen letter comes before the rest in the answer

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for queen, from Latin regina

indicators.note: crook means bent or out of order, so the letters of nastiest are rearranged

explanation.surface: The queen is unmoved by the vilest criminal stalking her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a noun for the criminal but is the anagram signal; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resistant withstands attack or influence, so it is impervious.

clue.text: Journalist completes review as Spurs get beaten

indicators.note: the journalist's letters complete the answer, coming at the end
to review is to go over again, here re-viewing the letters in a new order

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A sports writer finishes a match report on Tottenham Hotspur losing.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club. 'review' rearranges AS SPURS into SURPASS.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass someone is to outdo them, so surpassed means bettered or beaten.

clue.text: Will, the writer touring Italy, recalled travels

indicators.note: called back, so the whole is read in reverse
touring means going around, so the writer's surname goes round the Italy letter

parts.note: Will Self is an English novelist
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Novelist Will Self, on a tour of Italy, remembers his journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a testament or verb but is the first name of Will Self.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly is to travel by air, so flies is a synonym of travels.

clue.text: Battle — scared? 60% run away

indicators.note: the run letter goes away, leaving the rest
sixty per cent of a ten-letter word keeps only its first six letters

parts.note: scared means frightened
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A battle in which most of the frightened troops flee.
explanation.walkthrough: Keeping the first six of FRIGHTENED's ten letters gives FRIGHT; 'away' then drops R.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight is a combat or conflict, so it is a synonym of battle.

clue.text: Arrested over kind of tyres

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters of arrested are rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver is arrested over the state of their tyres.
explanation.definitionFit: Retreads are old tyres given a new tread, a cheaper type of tyre.

clue.text: Openings for medics to inhale O2

indicators.note: breathing in takes something inside, so the medics' letters go round the oxygen

parts.note: DRS is short for doctors, medics
O2 read as two Os

explanation.surface: Doctors open the way for patients to breathe oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: O2 is the formula for oxygen but here gives two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: Doors are the openings through which people enter rooms and buildings.

clue.text: Excited? Silver-plated goblet, two thirds off!

indicators.note: plating covers the outside, so the silver letters go around the goblet piece

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: removing two thirds of a six-letter word leaves its first two letters

explanation.surface: A thrilled cry at a silver-plated goblet going for a huge discount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two thirds off' sounds like a sale, but it cuts GOBLET to GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly expectant, so it describes someone excited.

clue.text: Remember to catch fish

indicators.note: to catch words is to hear them, so the fish's name is taken as heard

parts.note: plaice is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A reminder to go out and land a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' looks like angling, but it means hearing, the sense in 'I didn't catch what you said'.
explanation.definitionFit: To place someone is to recognise or recall who they are, as in I can't quite place her.

clue.text: Testing parking shelter

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
roofing is cover overhead, a shelter

explanation.surface: Checking a car park's covered shelter for faults.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof as in the proof of the pudding means a test, so proofing is testing.

clue.text: Bowl over after over, then departed following wicket

indicators.note: these letters follow the wicket letter, which comes first
one over letter comes after the other

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
D is the abbreviation for departed, as on timetables

explanation.surface: Cricket commentary: bowl over after over, then a batsman is out at the wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowl' looks like a cricket verb but is the noun: in the game of bowls the ball is called a wood.
explanation.definitionFit: In lawn bowls each bowl is traditionally called a wood, from the material it was made of.

clue.text: Adores wife's gold vessels

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife; the 's joins it to what follows
OR is gold in heraldry
ships are seagoing vessels

explanation.surface: A spouse's golden boats are much loved.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship someone is to revere and love them devotedly, so worships means adores.

clue.text: Sets of offices

definitions.meaning: to station troops is to set or place them in position
a station is a post or office someone holds, as in one's station in life

explanation.surface: Sets of offices, as in the suites of a business block.
explanation.definitionFit: Stations means places or posts, matching both setting in position and holding offices.

clue.text: Former US president loses millions, primarily tax dodger

indicators.note: the president's name loses that letter

parts.note: Harry Truman was US president from 1945 to 1953

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the first letter of tax is taken

explanation.surface: An ex-president loses millions and is chiefly a tax dodger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax dodger' reads as one phrase, but 'tax' gives only its first letter and 'dodger' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A truant is a pupil who skips school, someone dodging their lessons.

clue.text: Goes for recipe in pans

indicators.note: the recipe letter is put inside the pans word

parts.note: woks are Chinese cooking pans
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, seen on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A cook reaches for a recipe while working with pans.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that works is functioning, which is what goes means in the engine still goes.

clue.text: Stew — raw, yet tasteless

indicators.note: to stew is to cook the letters together into a new order

explanation.surface: A bland stew of raw ingredients, yet with no flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Watery food is thin and diluted, so it has little flavour and is tasteless.

clue.text: Sport's comeback following change passed on

indicators.note: a comeback turns things round, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: sport means fun, and the 's adds an S
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
to edit is to change a text

explanation.surface: A sporting comeback after a change of tactics passed on to the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Snuffed it is a slang idiom for dying, as is passed on.

clue.text: Face snooker revolution

definitions.meaning: a face, as of a cube
the spin put on a snooker ball by striking it off centre

explanation.surface: Facing up to a revolution in the game of snooker.
explanation.definitionFit: Side means a flat surface of a solid and also sidespin on a cue ball.

clue.text: Polish shoe with stockings

indicators.note: polishing works the letters over, so shoe is rearranged

explanation.surface: Buffing up a shoe along with the stockings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a shoe-care verb but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose is an old collective term for stockings and tights.

clue.text: Measure of bridge in Venice announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word for the bridge is pronounced

parts.note: the Bridge of Sighs is a famous bridge in Venice

explanation.surface: Someone announces the dimensions of a Venetian bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Size is the extent or dimensions of something, its measure.

clue.text: Base of guerrilla den in Ecuador revealed

indicators.note: the answer is revealed inside the run of words, spanning their boundaries

explanation.surface: A rebel hideout in Ecuador is uncovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' suggests the guerrilla camp, but it is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Adenine is one of the four nucleobases in DNA, so it is a base.

clue.text: Swinger's bar?

parts.note: suggests a nightclub for swingers, but means the bar an acrobat swings on

explanation.surface: A sly question about a club for swingers.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a horizontal bar hung on ropes, from which circus acrobats swing.
